The showroom itself is well-organized, modern, and easy to navigate, creating a pleasant environment for customers. featured_reviews.name: Onkar Tambe
featured_reviews.review_text:
My phone is a bit old and now it suddenly stops working, so I wanted to buy a new phone but since due to pandemic now online delivery of Mobile phones is not allowed in Maharashtra and hence, I approached local shops for buying a phone. I have been waiting for online delivery of mobile phones to start since more than 1.5 months, but the restrictions are still there and hence I cannot buy it online. When I approached local shops, they quoted extremely high price. I wanted to buy Redmi Note 10 Pro + Max, its price on amazon is Rs.20K and after applying card discount it can come down to Rs.18.5k, whereas these local shops quoted me prices like 21k and 22k and when I asked them for any discount, they denied it immediately. I communicated with these local shops using WhatsApp and phone calls. I received their number by looking at Mobile shops on google maps. So, I came across this “Jagdish Electronics” and I asked for the availability of the model and its price first he quoted me a price of Rs.20.8K and when I asked him for any discount he told “Come at shop, we will do whatever possible”. Well at this moment I hoped I will receive a discount of at least Rs.1,000 and if things went well, I would ask for even more discount. But things were not supposed to end well. He first offered me a discount of Rs.200, and I was amazed by this. When I tried to negotiate, he offered me additional discount of Rs.100. At this moment I was furious, he had the audacity to offer me a discount of Rs.300. What was he thinking, now-a-days if you want to buy a good cover for the mobile phone it can cost between Rs.300-Rs.500 and this person offers me a discount of Rs.300? It costed me more than Rs.100 to take a trip from home to that shop and back home. My face was red, and I could not hold my anger. He started telling me that he gets this mobile phone from the wholesaler at Rs.20k. And now he removed the cutter/blade from his drawer and started breaking the seal of the box, I stopped him and refused him to do so. He wasn’t ready to sell the phone at anything less than Rs.20.5K. Well, if my maths is correct, if he is selling the mobile phone at Rs.20.5k and he gets it at Rs.20K it means he is making a profit of Rs.500 [2.5% (absolute return)] on investment of Rs.20k, this is without considering the overhead expenses, direct cost and other expenses. A FD in Bank can fetch you a return of minimum 5% for 1 year. I do not know how many people have fallen for a trap like this and how many of them paid them extra money from their pockets, unnecessarily.
In the end I left without buying the mobile phone.

Conclusion: These people are not honest with their business; I wonder how they are going to retain customers by selling lies.
